Another year, another chance for the trucking industry to focus on brake safety. Let’s go over what fleets and drivers need to know for this year’s Brake Safety Week.

According to the Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance , Brake Safety Week is a commercial motor vehicle and driver inspection and regulatory compliance enforcement initiative, a brake-safety awareness and outreach opportunity, and a brake-related inspection and violation data collection project. Each year, this event is hosted by CVSA.

This means that inspections will be conducted throughout Brake Safety Week with particular focus on brake performance. Vehicles can be taken out of service if brake violations are discovered.

Brake Safety Week this year will be August 25-31. According to past CVSA records, Brake Safety Week typically occurs at the end of August.

Unlike Brake Safety Day , another CVSA event—the date of which goes unannounced until after the event has occurred—fleets have time and the knowledge needed to prepare for Brake Safety Week.

How should fleets prepare for Brake Safety Week?

The emphasis of Brake Safety Week this year will be on the condition of brake linings and pads. Inspectors will be looking for excessive wear in the brake linings and pads, particularly cracks, according to Jim Ward, senior safety manager at Transervice Logistics .

Ward said that one red flag that drivers may not think twice about but inspectors will is rubbing air lines.

“Those [rubbing air lines] get written up a lot,” Ward said. “If you have two brake lines—which some of them are rubber, others are like a poly material—what happens is those two hoses have a lot of pressure going through them, and they're sitting right next to each other. So over time, with the vibration of the truck, they tend to rub against each other, and they can start leaving little marks on each other. Sometimes they'll wear down far enough to actually put a big chafe into the hose. To me, that's something that's overlooked. It may look fine, but if those two hoses are touching, you're going to get written up for it because you should make sure that they’re kept separated.”

See also: CVSA releases results of 2024 Brake Safety Day

To prepare for Brake Safety Week, Ward suggests focusing on pre- and post-trip inspections as well as preventive maintenance .

“The most important thing is PM and pre-trip inspections,” Ward said. “Make sure that the trucks are PM’d on a regular basis … When you're a driver, the most important thing for you to continue to do is pre-trip. Pre-trip inspect your vehicle because it saves your life and the people in front of you or people around you.”

What will the results of Brake Safety Week be?

According to CVSA, Brake Safety Week in 2022 resulted in 13.3% out-of-service violations. This decreased to 12.6% in 2023. This trend may continue in 2024, however, it’s also possible that safety technology will result in more accurate brake performance inspections.

This year, CVSA announced that performance-based brake testers (PBBTs) will be used in some jurisdictions during Brake Safety Week. PBBTs are machines that test brake performance. They measure the slow-speed brake force and weight at each wheel of a vehicle, add up the total vehicle brake force, and divide it by the total vehicle weight to determine overall vehicle braking efficiency.

It’s difficult to speculate, but the use of this technology could affect the percentage of out-of-service violations with more accurate measurements of brake performance.

According to CVSA, brake violations comprise the largest percentage of out-of-service violations cited during roadside inspections. CVSA cites that in last year’s International Roadcheck , brake violations were the top vehicle violation, comprising 25.2% of all vehicle out-of-service violations during those three days.

Brake Safety Week serves as a reminder to drivers and fleet managers of the importance of vehicle maintenance and provides an opportunity for law enforcement to highlight the importance of brake safety for all.

Nuclear verdicts and lawsuit abuse are pushing insurance costs beyond reach.

Poor maintenance, weak driver vetting, and compliance gaps can quickly turn accidents into multimillion-dollar courtroom losses.

Safety technology and proactive risk management are becoming essential tools to reduce crashes, limit liability, and protect fleet viability.

America relies on the trucking industry to keep shelves stocked and commerce moving. But behind the scenes, motor carriers and their insurers are fighting for survival against an escalating threat: lawsuit abuse and the surge of nuclear verdicts reshaping the legal landscape.

Excessive litigation and runaway jury awards have turned even minor accidents into existential financial risks. The federally mandated $750,000 insurance minimum—unchanged since the 1980s—is now a fraction of what a single serious claim can cost. No carrier is safe when settlements routinely reach into the tens of millions, particularly small and midsized fleets.

Worse still, trucking companies often shoulder the blame even when passenger vehicles cause the crash. A reckless driver cutting off a semi can still result in a jury placing the bulk of responsibility—and the financial fallout—on the carrier.

In September 2025, the Chamber of Commerce Institute for Legal Reform (ILR) published an article that detailed just how damaging this practice is and what should be done to combat it. The article noted that a 2023 study of 154 trucking litigation verdicts for accidents occurring between June 2020 and April 2023 found “an average winning plaintiffs’ award of over $27 million before repeals or reduction.”

In this same vein, data from the American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) tracked verdicts from 2010 to 2018. They found that average verdicts of $5 million in 2010 surged to $23.5 million by 2018, and that has continued to grow. What is truly troubling is that the number of high-dollar awards often bears little correlation to actual medical costs and is treated as non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering. According to the ILR, “in six out of the 10 years in our research, economic damages accounted for more than the combined total value of economic and punitive damages in nuclear verdicts for which a breakdown of damages was available.”

For an industry already operating on razor-thin margins, the combination of nuclear verdicts, litigation abuse, higher insurance premiums, and operational challenges is creating a financial pressure cooker.

Under no circumstances do I want to imply that accidents involving commercial trucks and passenger vehicles are never the truck driver’s responsibility. However, carriers still bear the burden even when they are not at fault. Until we have the appropriate tort reform, fleets will have to do what they can to reduce accidents and mitigate damages.

1. Maintenance is your first defense against catastrophic claims

Mechanical failures are a plaintiff attorney’s best friend—and a carrier’s worst nightmare.

The 2025 Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance (CVSA) International Roadcheck revealed troubling statistics:

41% of vehicle out-of-service violations were brake-related

Let’s face it, a single failed brake chamber or worn tire can transform a defensible case into a jackpot for plaintiffs.

To reduce exposure, fleets must commit to rigorous:

Preventive maintenance: Catching failures before they sideline a truck

Predictive maintenance: Using data to identify risks before they become violations

Anything less leaves carriers vulnerable not just to breakdowns but also to devastating courtroom outcomes.

Fleets Explained: What are nuclear verdicts?

Clark: Nuclear verdicts and rising insurance premiums put fleets at risk

2. Drivers are a carrier’s greatest asset and its biggest legal risk

Human error remains a leading cause of trucking litigation. The 2025 Roadcheck highlighted persistent issues (these stats include the U.S. and Canada):

Hours-of-service violations remain the top driver-related OOS issue.

Nearly 25% of drivers inspected lacked a valid CDL.

Dozens of violations involved drug and alcohol use.

In court, these gaps become narrative fuel for plaintiff attorneys eager to paint carriers as negligent.

Zero-tolerance drug and alcohol policies

But with a nationwide driver shortage, companies often face impossible choices: Hire underqualified drivers or miss revenue opportunities. Unfortunately, juries don’t care about staffing shortages; they care about whether you hired a driver who shouldn’t have been behind the wheel.

3. Technology is a powerful shield against nuclear verdicts

Advanced safety technology won’t eliminate all accidents, but it can dramatically reduce both incident frequency and courtroom exposure.

Injury-causing truck crashes could drop 23% with modern safety systems.

Forward collision mitigation reduces front-end crashes by 44%.

Systems like automatic emergency braking, lane departure warnings, and onboard cameras don’t just save lives; they save carriers from litigation disasters.

These technologies are expensive, and many small fleets can’t afford the upfront cost. Still, the investment often pales in comparison to the financial destruction of a nuclear verdict. Data showing proactive safety measures can significantly reduce damages or even shift liability.

Nuclear verdicts and predatory litigation threaten the long-term stability not only of individual carriers but also of the insurance market itself. If premiums keep climbing and verdicts keep multiplying, insurers will retreat, carriers will close, and supply chains will suffer.

Carriers that take proactive steps today stand the best chance of weathering an increasingly hostile legal environment.

As advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) become more common and complex, repairers and insurers need trusted calibration guidance at the point of decision.

“The growing complexity of today’s vehicles is raising the stakes for every participant in the repair ecosystem,” said Dan Risley, vice president, Automotive Services Group for CCC. “Supporting safe, proper and consistent repairs requires collaboration across repairers, insurers, automakers, diagnostics providers and technology partners. CCC is helping make trusted calibration guidance easier to access and apply as repair and claims decisions are being made.”

Industry stakeholders, including leading repair associations and consumer advocacy groups, have increasingly identified ADAS calibrations as one of the collision repair industry’s most pressing issues, citing the need for easier access to trusted repair guidance.

“ADAS represents one of the most significant technological changes our industry has ever faced,” said Erick Bickett, director, PACE Calibration Centers. “The pace and magnitude of this change demand collaboration across the entire industry. We appreciate CCC’s leadership in making calibration guidance more accessible at the point where critical repair decisions are made and for their work as part of CIECA’s ADAS Calibration Committee. Together, these efforts are important steps toward greater transparency and proper repairers.”

CCC’s Calibration Guidelines sources recommendations, informed by vehicle manufacturers’ repair and calibration requirements, from leading calibration and diagnostics providers. Current participants include asTech (via adasThink), Azimuth, Opus (via ADAS Map Pro), Kinetic and REVV.

“No single stakeholder can solve this challenge alone,” Risley said. “The industry’s continued focus on ADAS calibration reflects a shared commitment to consumers, safer roadways and the proper repair of increasingly sophisticated vehicles. CCC is proud to support those efforts by helping connect trusted information with the people who need it.”

Calibration Guidelines is available to all CCC ONE users at no additional cost from CCC. Customers with a contracted participating provider can access recommendations through the Diagnostics button in CCC ONE; insurers using Advanced or Intelligent Estimating in APEX can also access the capability.

Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen celebrated the opening of a new automotive career training center at Central Community College’s Hastings Campus earlier this week.

“This is a significant investment in Nebraska’s future, giving more students the opportunity to gain hands-on training, develop valuable skills, and build rewarding careers right here in our state,” Pillen said in a social media post .

The new Gosper Building will house automotive technology and autobody programs, according to a post made by Central Community College .

The $20 million, 42,000 square-foot building will replace the college’s old facility, which had limitations to industry training methods, local news station NTV says .

“The program over the last couple of years has been growing. Every single year we’ve had, we’ve seen more enrollment, higher enrollment. So we needed to expand our capacity for tools, equipment and instruction.” First Year Automotive Instructor Nick Kelley told NTV.  “There’s an increased interest in automotive technology, cars are getting more technologically advanced so we need better training and more training. There’s still people that really like, really enjoy working on cars.”

The new building can hold 70 automotive students and 20 autobody students, the news station reports. The college offers certifications, diplomas and associate degrees in automotive technology, Auto body technology and other fields.

“I could not be more proud of what our community colleges do for workforce development and creating extraordinary careers – extraordinary careers that you can get developed, in some instances, certification in eight weeks,” NTV reports the Governor during the groundbreaking ceremony.

NTV previously reported that the facility will feature five new classrooms, a welding lab and capacity to work on electric vehicles and modern technology.

The U.S. economy is short roughly 140,000 skilled technicians a year , and the gap is widening, with 73,354 new collision repair entrant technicians needed by 2029, according to the TechForce Foundation’s new “Technician Supply, Demand & Opportunity Report.”

Across those 10 sectors, employers will need 241,842 new technicians per year through 2029, the report finds, compared with 101,743 students who graduated from technical schools and community colleges last year. TechForce found that the collision repair sector sees the highest turnover of the 10 analyzed at 60.7%.

The 2004-2013 Mazda 3 is based on the Ford global C1 platform, shared with the European Ford Focus and Volvo S40. Nothing is really groundbreaking about the mechanical brake system, but not paying attention to the details can end in a post-brake-job comeback.

A key service issue concerns the hydraulics and ABS system. The older the car, the greater the chance the brake fluid has not been serviced. Over time this can cause issues with the ABS hydraulic control unit.

For almost 10 years, Mazda used the same caliper, pad and rotor design. Pads should be replaced when there is 2mm or less of friction material. If the rotors are any thicker, they have enough material on them to last at least one turning on the lathe. The runout specification for these vehicles is .002” and disc thickness variation should be far below .0005”.

Mazda claims repeated panic braking may raise the temperature in some portions of the disc plate by approx. 1,000°C (l,832°F). This temperature is almost near impossible to achieve this side of a high-speed police chase.

The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 75 ft./lbs.

All Mazda3 models have rear disc brakes. The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 55 ft./lbs.

Mazda uses a hand brake that is incorporated into the rear caliper, and a couple of systems are employed to retract rear pistons. The later-model cars require the familiar method of turning the piston clockwise while applying pressure, where others will have a plug on the back side of the caliper that provides access for an Allen wrench to facilitate retracting the piston. Be careful as you retract the piston.

After the pads are replaced, pump the pedal and adjust the parking brake mechanism in the rear calipers. If the level has too much travel, perform the following steps:

Remove the service hole cover of the rear console.

Turn the adjusting nut and adjust the parking brake lever.

After adjustment, pull the parking brake lever one notch and verify that the parking brake warning light illuminates and the rear brakes do not drag.

The Mazda3 comes in two styles, ABS and ABS with Dynamic Stability Control (DSC). Both systems connect to other vehicle components via a high-speed serial data bus. The DSC system ties more components together (like a yaw/pitch sensor and steering position sensor) onto the bus.

If you are seeing communication-related DTCs, it is essential that you fully diagnose problems with the system before you start replacing sensors and modules. Some of these vehicles have been on the road for more than six years and the connections will be starting to corrode and fret.

One of the main facilitators of ABS/DCS problems are the connectors, especially under the hood where the control/modulator unit connects. Being able to measure values at the connectors and observe data on a scan tool is essential for diagnosing problems.

The biggest ABS issue with the three generations of Mazda 3 is power. With some higher mileage vehicles, the battery cables, wiring from the power distribution box or the ground connection (behind the driver’s side headlight at G02) can have enough resistance so the voltage drops below 8 volts. When this happens, the ABS module cuts control and the electronic brake distribution system is disabled.

If a modulator/control unit is replaced, the pressure sensors must be recalibrated with a scan tool that is able to communicate with the chassis/ABS module. If this is not performed, it can result in brake failure and lock up.

If you have DTCs C1141, C1142, C1143, C1144, C1233, C1234, C1235 or C1236 (ABS wheel-speed sensor/ABS sensor rotor), chances are something is wrong with the wheel bearings. Another cause for these codes could be an accumulation of metal debris on the sensor. The front bearings are press-in cartridge-style units. Rear wheel bearings are hub units. In the front, the tone ring, or encoder, is on the inner seal of the bearing and the sensor is mounted in the knuckle. The parameters for these codes to be set include abnormalities in the signal such as a weak signal or large differences in the value when compared to the other sensors.

If you have DTCs C1145, C1155, C1165 or C1175 (open sensor), it could be damaged wiring or a failed sensor that is the problem. If you have more than one, chances are there is a problem with the connection at the control unit or in the front or rear harnesses of the sensors.

These DTCs will usually clear themselves after repairs are made and the vehicle is driven above 6.2 mph when the self-diagnostic check is performed.

Some customers may report a slight clunk, bang or jolt from the front of the vehicle. This concern will most likely occur during the vehicle’s first forward movement and after the vehicle sits for a few hours and/or a cold soak. This is a normal operating noise of the ABS system.

If you encounter a customer complaint for this concern, explain that the noise comes from the ABS/TCS/DSC “Malfunction Detection Function” initial check. The initial check is a necessary function to ensure the normal operation of the ABS/TCS/DSC system. The fifth-generation Ram 2500 places substantial demands on its brakes. Many of these trucks carry heavy payloads, tow trailers or operate in fleets, so a successful brake job requires a complete-system inspection and parts that match the platform’s thermal and mechanical demands.

- Modern Maintenance Requires More Than Checking Mileage

This Brake Job covers the 2019-present fifth-generation Ram 2500, not the Ram 1500. The 2500 uses heavy-duty components and platform-specific procedures. Confirm the model year, engine, axle and options before ordering parts or applying specifications.

The Ram 2500 has four-wheel vented discs and dual-piston sliding calipers. Separate parking-brake shoes act against a drum surface inside each rear rotor hat.

Booster configuration depends on the engine. The 6.4L Hemi uses a dual-diaphragm vacuum booster and an electric vacuum pump near the left front of the engine to supplement engine vacuum. The PCM commands the pump based on operating inputs. The 6.7L diesel uses Hydro-Boost, supplied by the power-steering pump, with an accumulator providing limited reserve assist if pump pressure is lost.

When it’s practical, begin the process with a road test and note pedal travel, assist, pull, vibration and noise under normal braking. Confirm the complaint before disassembly; a vibration blamed on the front brakes may originate at the rear, and an assist complaint may come from the vacuum or power-steering circuit rather than the foundation brakes.

Clean around the master-cylinder cap and verify that the fluid is at the MAX mark. On a diesel vehicle, you should also inspect the power-steering fluid level, hoses and lines, because Hydro-Boost depends on that circuit. Low fluid, leaks, restrictions or weak pump output can create assist complaints. On gasoline models, inspect booster vacuum plumbing and electric-pump operation.

Compare inner and outer pad wear and both sides of each axle. Uneven wear can reveal seized hardware, binding pads, piston trouble or slide problems. Replace pads as an axle set if usable lining at the thinnest point is 1 mm (0.04 inch) or less. Inspect boots, pistons, slides, hoses and bleeders for damage, leakage and corrosion.

Be sure to measure the rotors. Minimum thickness is 37.4 mm (1.47 inches) front and 32.4 mm (1.28 inches) rear. Maximum runout is 0.020 mm (0.0008 inch); maximum loose-rotor thickness variation is 0.008 mm (0.00031 inch). You should also inspect the internal parking-brake surface; maximum drum diameter is 207.2 mm (8.157 inches).

Support the caliper and adapter; never let the hose carry their weight. Clean the pad lands and hub face without removing base metal. Install new anti-rattle clips, verify free pad movement and make sure both pistons retract smoothly. Because the rotor fits over the hub studs, hub cleanliness and uniform wheel-fastener torque are critical to controlling installed runout.

Rear service adds the parking-brake assembly. A rotor that will not release may be hanging on the shoes, so release the pedal and back off the star wheel if necessary. With the rotor off, inspect the shoes, springs, adjuster, cable action and drum surface. Clean the hub and bracket, verify piston and slide movement, and install new hardware and sealing washers as required.

Always replace caliper hardware; old clips can restrict pad movement and cause uneven wear.

Use fresh fluid meeting SAE J1703-F and DOT 3 standards. Bleed in this order: right rear, left rear, right front and left front, keeping the reservoir full. For pressure bleeding, use the correct adapter; 15-20 PSI is generally sufficient, depending on equipment limits.

If air entered the HCU, perform a base bleed, use a capable scan tool’s ABS Miscellaneous menu to run the HCU bleed routine, then bleed the base system again. Set the fluid level and verify a firm pedal.

Hydro-Boost is generally self- bleeding. Fill the power-steering reservoir, disable the engine and crank it for several seconds, then recheck the level. Re-enable and start the engine, slowly turn lock to lock twice, shut it off and discharge the accumulator with five pedal applications. Restart, repeat two slow lock-to-lock cycles, shut down and correct the level. If the fluid foams, let it dissipate before repeating the final cycles.

Adjust the shoes before cable tension. With the pedal fully released and the front cable slackened at the frame-rail adjuster, turn each star wheel through the backing-plate hole until slight drag is felt, then back it off until drag disappears. Adjust both sides equally.

Cable-tensioner adjustment is normally required only after replacement or disconnection. After verifying cable movement and shoe adjustment, fully apply the pedal. Mark the non-threaded tensioner rod 1/4 inch from the tensioner edge and tighten the nut until the mark disappears. Release the pedal, confirm both wheels rotate freely, verify that the brake holds and road-test the truck.

Drawing on its experience developing and industrializing fuel cell technology, EKPO is advancing hydrogen use across various mobility applications. The HyFleet project illustrates how this technology can support demanding specialty vehicle applications. BRP-Rotax developed the side-by-side vehicle in collaboration with industry and research partners. The vehicle offers a range of up to 400 kilometers and a refueling time of approximately five minutes.

- TISAX: What Global Automotive Suppliers Need to Know

- AUMOVIO, Chery Partner to Localize European Auto Production

- Schaeffler, Qorix Partner on Software-Defined Vehicle Platforms

Fuel Cell Technology Powers HyFleet Vehicle

EKPO’s high-performance NM12 stack forms the heart of the fuel cell system. The stack delivers high power density and supports the 90-kW fuel cell system. The system achieves an efficiency of up to 60% and responds rapidly to changes in load.

Extensive on- and off-road testing under real-world conditions demonstrates the system’s suitability for practical use.

EKPO collaborated with HyCentA to develop a passive hydrogen recirculation system that provides additional robustness and efficiency. An innovative two-step needle ejector reduces mechanical complexity.

The system also supports cold starts and freeze starts at temperatures as low as minus 20 degrees Celsius. These capabilities allow operation in winter and alpine conditions.

“HyFleet shows how we are applying our many years of fuel cell expertise to new mobility applications,” said Dr. Stefan Dwenger, managing director of EKPO Fuel Cell Technologies GmbH. “Hydrogen is particularly well suited to demanding on- and off-road applications that require long operating hours and high availability. Our NM12 fuel cell stack, backed by our expertise in development and industrialization, helps our partners put this potential to work.”

HyFleet Tests Hydrogen Applications Under Real-World Conditions

The HyFleet initiative tests this technology under real-world operating conditions. The project generates insights into hydrogen-powered specialty vehicles for agriculture, forestry, tourism, municipal services and industry, among other sectors.

HyFleet takes an integrated approach to operating hydrogen-powered vehicle fleets. The project considers every stage, from local green hydrogen production to the powertrain, vehicle and scalable refueling infrastructure. The results also help guide further development and the technology’s use in additional applications.

“HyFleet has demonstrated that a hydrogen fuel cell powertrain can also work successfully in a compact special-purpose vehicle designed for off-road use,” said Stefan Arndt, general manager BRP-Rotax, VP R&D Powertrain. “In EKPO, we have a partner that brought extensive experience in developing and industrializing fuel cell stacks to the project, along with technology tailored to our needs. EKPO thus played a key role in turning our vehicle concept into reality.”

EKPO to Showcase Fuel Cell Portfolio at Hydrogen Technology World Expo 2026

EKPO brings more than 20 years of fuel cell technology experience to its development and industrialization capabilities. The company draws on its automotive industry experience to develop fuel cell solutions. Alongside HyFleet, EKPO will showcase fuel cell stacks and components for mobile and stationary applications at the event in Hamburg.

The modular platforms offer power outputs ranging from 16 kW to more than 400 kW. Their designs emphasize high power density, efficiency and reliable operation. EKPO also develops customized stack solutions that meet each customer’s system architecture and specific requirements.

EKPO Develops Components for Green Hydrogen Production

EKPO’s portfolio extends to green hydrogen production. The company develops and manufactures metal bipolar plates for proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers. EKPO applies its expertise in precision forming, coating and sealing technologies to meet the specific demands of electrolysis. The company designs the bipolar plates to withstand demanding operating conditions and support scalable industrial manufacturing.

Proceeds support WACOSA programs that provide meaningful employment, day services and opportunities for more than 650 adults with disabilities across central Minnesota.

The event began with a walleye shore lunch and guided tours of WACOSA before attendees gathered at APH’s newest facility (a bulk storage warehouse) in St. Cloud for a pie and ice cream social celebrating its grand opening and APH’s “Building Our Future Together” initiative.

The day concluded with a cocktail reception, lobster-themed dinner and awards ceremony hosted by John and Nancy Bartlett at their home. A highlight of the evening was the presentation of a $513,000 check to Nancy Betts, executive director of WACOSA.

“Fourteen years of support from APH, its supplier partners and the Bartlett family has created a remarkable legacy for the people we serve,” Betts said. “This generosity creates opportunities for people to discover their strengths, contribute to their communities and pursue greater independence. Corey Bartlett, CEO and owner of APH, said the event reflects the generosity and commitment of the automotive aftermarket community.

Imagine being a belt on the front of the engine. Yours is a balancing act that is always being upset by change from the inputs from the crank pulley and the loads from the alternator, AC compressor and maybe a power steering pump. Your mission is to keep in contact with the grooves on the pulleys. You can’t hold on too tightly, because it could decrease fuel economy and damage the bearings inside the water pump, idler bushings and other components. But you can’t be too loose because it will cause you to slip, resulting in wear and noise.

- What Sets a Slow-Response O2 or Air/Fuel Sensor Code?

- Six Tips for Building and Selling a Better Timing Belt Job

- How Modules Manage Electrical and Mechanical Loads

A serpentine belt transfers torque through friction between its ribs and the pulley grooves. The belt must be held tightly enough against the pulleys to prevent slipping under the system’s maximum expected expected load.

As mentioned before, if tension is too low, the belt can microslip or visibly slip. This generates heat, polishes the belt ribs and pulley grooves, and may produce a chirp or squeal. Slippage can also reduce alternator output, power steering assist, coolant-pump speed or AC compressor performance.

Excessive tension creates a different set of problems. Every accessory shaft experiences a radial load from the belt. Raising belt tension increases that load, which can accelerate bearing wear in the alternator, water pump, idlers, tensioner and AC compressor. It also increases belt fatigue as the belt repeatedly bends around the pulleys. The additional bearing friction and belt deformation represent a small but measurable parasitic loss.

The correct tension is consequently the lowest tension that can reliably transmit the required torque under all operating conditions. That reduces friction and improves efficiency while preserving traction and controlling noise.

An automatic tensioner’s spring applies the required static tension, while an internal damping mechanism controls rapid arm movement. The damping prevents the tensioner from bouncing in response to engine firing pulses and accessory-load changes. Insufficient tension causes slippage, heat and noise, while excessive tension contributes to accessory wear. Some belt companies tensioner guidance also identifies excessive arm oscillation as a sign of a failed damping system or another drive-system problem.

What Happens When Accessory Load Increases?

The belt does not have identical tension everywhere around its path. When the crankshaft is driving an accessory, the belt span pulling the accessory pulley becomes the tight side. The belt leaving that pulley has less tension. The difference between those forces, combined with pulley radius, produces the torque that turns the accessory.

When alternator electrical output increases, electromagnetic resistance inside the alternator rises. The crankshaft must supply more torque through the belt. The tension difference across the alternator pulley increases, and the belt may elongate elastically by a very small amount. The tensioner moves to manage that change.

A hydraulic power steering pump produces a similar reaction when the driver turns the steering wheel, especially near the steering stop. Pump pressure and required input torque rise rapidly. On systems with belt-driven AC compressors, compressor engagement can create an even sharper load change.

These loads are why a belt drive may operate quietly in the bay but squeal when the headlights, blower motor and rear defroster are switched on, when the steering wheel is turned at idle or when the AC compressor engages. The added load exposes marginal tension, worn ribs, pulley contamination or misalignment.

Technicians should reproduce the operating condition instead of judging the drive only at unloaded idle.

Engine-Speed Changes and Tension Reversals

Crankshaft speed is not perfectly constant. Each combustion event accelerates the crankshaft, while compression strokes and drivetrain events slow it. Those variations become more pronounced during startup, shutdown, throttle changes, transmission shifts and cylinder-deactivation transitions.

During acceleration, the belt must accelerate the rotating mass of every accessory. The alternator is particularly important because its rotor normally turns several times faster than the crankshaft. Its inertia resists a sudden increase in belt speed.

During rapid engine deceleration, the situation changes. The alternator rotor wants to continue spinning and can momentarily drive against the decelerating belt. The normal tight- and slack-side relationship does not permanently swap during ordinary operation, because the crankshaft remains the primary power source. However, local belt forces can equalize or briefly reverse during a transient event. The tensioner arm may then move sharply as the tension disturbance travels through the drive.

This can produce intermittent chirps, belt slap or tensioner rattle that does not occur at steady engine speed. A noise heard only during startup, shutdown, throttle tip-in or a downshift is therefore an important diagnostic clue.

Many late-model applications use an overrunning alternator pulley or overrunning alternator decoupler  (OAD) to control these events. The pulley allows the alternator to overrun the belt during rapid deceleration. An OAD also uses an internal torsion spring to absorb speed and tension fluctuations. This arrangement reduces vibration and allows the alternator to freewheel during deceleration.

A seized decoupler can act like a solid pulley, causing excessive tensioner movement and a chirp during startup or shutdown. Installing a solid pulley where an OAD was specified can create noise and shorten belt and tensioner life.

Why Replace the Belt and Tensioner Together?

This episode of DriveTime features Scott Howat, director of sales and marketing, Litens Aftermarket N.A.

- Automotive Parts Services Group CEO Jeff Koviak on Multiplying Successes

- MotoRad CEO Matt Buchholz on Aligning Values

- Continental Tire’s Brian Beierwaltes on Driving Brand Promise

Howat said the company’s engineering-driven approach is what differentiates its belt drive tensioners. With a history of innovation dating back to its founder’s invention of the first belt tensioner in 1979, Litens has developed an extensive portfolio of patented technologies. Unlike manufacturers focused primarily on individual components, Litens engineers complete belt drive systems, with the tensioner and pulley system playing a central role in their operation. Howat emphasized that this engineering expertise and problem-solving approach allow Litens to deliver innovative tensioning solutions to the aftermarket.

Howat outlined Litens ‘ strategy for integrating Dolz into its aftermarket portfolio, following its acquisition of the European water pump manufacturer about three years ago. Building on the approach used to establish the Litens brand in North America, the company is taking a phased approach to introducing Dolz to the market and building brand awareness. Howat, who oversees the company’s North American sales and marketing operations, said the strategy includes a marketing campaign launched this year, with plans to formally introduce the Dolz brand at AAPEX.

Litens’ ability to translate OE engineering expertise into aftermarket innovation begins with its extensive OE product knowledge and data, Howat explained. This expertise also enables the company to identify opportunities to improve upon existing OE designs.

As an example, Howat highlighted Litens’ newly patented Easy Button Latch technology, which simplifies tensioner installation by incorporating the locking mechanism directly into the component. The innovation eliminates installation challenges associated with conventional locking pins. It demonstrates how Litens leverages its engineering capabilities to develop aftermarket solutions that deliver practical benefits to technicians.

• How Litens’ engineering expertise and patented tensioner technologies differentiate its belt drive systems. (5:00)

• How Litens is integrating Dolz into its portfolio and building brand awareness in the North American aftermarket. (6:53)

• Litens leverages OE engineering expertise and data to develop innovative aftermarket solutions. (8:30)

• Litens’ patented Easy Button Latch technology simplifies tensioner installation for technicians. (9:36)

• Lightning Round: Howat shares some personal insights. (11:24)

This episode of DriveTime features Jeff Koviak, CEO, Automotive Parts Services Group.

- MotoRad CEO Matt Buchholz on Aligning Values

- Litens Aftermarket’s Scott Howat on Being a Brand Champion

- Continental Tire’s Brian Beierwaltes on Driving Brand Promise

Koviak said he views industry consolidation as an inevitable evolution that can ultimately make the independent aftermarket stronger and more competitive. Rather than becoming “distracted by the noise,” he believes Automotive Parts Services Group members should remain focused on running their businesses and getting their parts through the supply chain and installed onto cars. Koviak sees consolidation creating stronger organizations through investment and greater efficiencies, helping the independent aftermarket compete more effectively with OEM service centers.

Koviak said collaboration and shared innovation represent one of The Group’s greatest opportunities to help members grow while preserving their entrepreneurial spirit. His focus as CEO includes bringing members together through collaborative workshops where they can exchange best practices and learn from one another. While building trust takes time, Koviak added that members are increasingly recognizing the value of working together. He believes closer collaboration can multiply growth opportunities and strengthen The Group and its members.

Koviak also sees data and technology as critical competitive advantages. The Group is investing in IT best-practices workshops and industry technology initiatives to identify cost-saving opportunities and share innovative approaches across its membership. Koviak said The Group’s extensive North American DIFM market data can help members optimize inventory and make smarter business decisions while supporting closer collaboration with supplier partners on supply chain needs. Ultimately, the goal is to maximize that data to improve product availability and get the right parts where they are needed.

To hear more of Koviak’s insights, be sure to watch the above video.

证券代码：002590 证券简称：万安科技 公告编号：2026-051 浙江万安科技股份有限公司 关于公司开展资产池业务的公告 本公司及董事会全体成员保证信息披露内容的真实、准确、完整，没有虚假记载、误导性陈述或重大遗漏。 浙江万安科技股份有限公司（以下简称“公司”）于 2026 年 8 月 27 日召开第 七届董事会第二次会议，会议审议通过了《关于公司开展资产池业务的议案》，同意公司及合并报表范围内子公司开展资产池业务，额度不超过 5 亿元人民币，资产池业务的开展期限为自股东会审议通过本议案之日起 3 年，在业务期限内，上述额度可以循环滚动使用。该事项尚需提交公司股东会审议，具体情况如下： 一、资产池业务情况概述 1、业务概述 资产池业务是指协议银行为满足公司对所拥有的资产进行统一管理、统筹使用的需要，向公司提供的资产管理与融资服务等功能于一体的综合金融服务平台，是协议银行对企业提供流动性服务的主要载体。 资产池入池资产是指公司合法拥有的，向协议银行申请管理或进入资产池进行质押的权利或流动资产，包括银行授信、存单、承兑汇票、信用证、理财产品、应收账款等。 资产池项下的票据池业务是指协议银行对入池的纸质汇票及电子商业汇票进行统一管理、统筹使用，向公司提供的集票据托管和托收、票据代理查询、票据贴现、票据质押池融资、业务统计等功能于一体的票据综合管理服务。同时公司接受银行对公司的授信额度，利用此授信额度为本公司办理开具银行承兑汇票等业务用于支付采购款或融资等相关银行业务。 2、合作机构 公司拟根据实际情况及具体合作条件选择国内资信良好的商业银行或其他金融机构作为资产池业务的合作金融机构，具体协议银行提请公司股东会授权公司管理层根据公司及子公司与商业银行的合作关系，商业银行资产池服务能力等综合因素选择。 3、业务期限 资产池业务的开展期限为自股东会审议通过之日起 3 年。 4、实施额度 公司及子公司共享不超过 5 亿元的资产池额度。业务期限内，该额度可滚动使用。具体每笔发生额提请公司股东会授权公司管理层根据公司和子公司的经营需要按照系统利益最大化原则确定。 5、担保方式 在风险可控的前提下，公司及合并报表范围内子公司可以根据需要为资产池的建立和使用采用最高额质押、一般质押、存单质押、票据质押、保证金质押等多种担保方式进行担保。具体担保形式及金额根据公司经营需要具体确定及办理，但不得超过资产池业务额度。 在开展资产池业务过程中，如涉及公司为子公司提供担保、子公司为子公司提供担保、子公司为公司提供担保等担保情形，担保总额度不超过人民币 5 亿元，业务期限内，该额度可滚动使用。 二、开展资产池业务的目的 公司及子公司将银行授信、存单、承兑汇票、信用证、理财产品、应收账款等金融资产存入协议银行进行集中管理，办理金融资产入池、出池以及质押融资等业务和服务，可有效地盘活金融资产、减少资金占用，提高公司流动资产的使用效率，有利于补充公司流动资金缺口实现公司及股东权益的最大化。 三、资产池业务的风险与风险控制 1、流动性风险 公司开展资产池业务，需在合作金融机构开立资产池质押融资业务专项保证金账户，作为资产池项下质押资产到期托收回款的入账账户。入池质押资产和开立的有价票证到期日期不一致的情况会导致托收资金进入公司申请开立的保证金账户，对公司资金的流动性有一定影响。 风险控制措施：公司可以通过用新增资产入池置换保证金方式解除这一影响，资金流动性风险可控。 2、业务模式风险 公司以进入资产池的存单、票据等作质押，向合作金融机构申请开具商业汇票、信用证等有价票证，用于支付供应商货款等经营发生的款项，随着质押票据的到期，办理托收解付，若票据到期不能正常托收，所质押担保的票据额度不足，导致合作金融机构可能要求公司追加担保。 风险控制措施：公司与合作金融机构开展资产池业务后，公司将安排专人与合作金融机构对接，建立资产池台账、跟踪管理，及时了解到期有价票证托收解付情况和安排公司新收有价票证入池，保证入池有价票证的安全和流动性。 四、决策程序和组织实施 1、在上述业务期限及额度范围内，提请股东会授权公司管理层行使具体操作的决策权并签署相关合同文件，包括但不限于选择合格的金融机构、确定公司及子公司可以使用的资产池具体额度、担保物及担保形式、金额等。 2、授权公司财务资金管理人员负责组织实施资产池业务。公司财务资金管理人员将及时分析和跟踪资产池业务进展情况，如发现或判断有不利因素，将及时采取相应措施控制风险，并第一时间向公司董事会报告。 3、公司内部审计部门负责对资产池业务开展情况进行审计和监督。 4、独立董事有权对公司资产池业务的具体情况进行监督与检查。 特此公告。 浙江万安科技股份有限公司董事会 2026 年 8 月 27 日

 证券代码：002590 证券简称：万安科技 公告编号：2026-047 浙江万安科技股份有限公司 关于完成董事会换届选举并聘任高级管理人员、 证券事务代表的公告 本公司及董事会全体成员保证本公告内容真实、准确和完整，没有任何虚假记载、误导性陈述或者重大遗漏。 浙江万安科技股份有限公司（以下简称“公司”）于2026年6月8日召开2026年第二次临时股东会，会议审议通过了《关于换届选举非独立董事的议案》《关于换届选举独立董事的议案》，选举产生了5名非独立董事和3名独立董事，与公司职工代表大会选举产生的1名职工代表董事共同组成公司第七届董事会。同日，公司召开了第七届董事会第一次会议，会议选举产生了第七届董事会董事长、董事会各专门委员会委员，并聘任了公司高级管理人员及证券事务代表。现将有关情况公告如下： 一、公司第七届董事会组成情况 非独立董事：陈锋先生（董事长）、傅直全先生、姚焕春先生、斯陈锋先生、 俞佳乐先生 独立董事：闫建来先生、吴小丽女士、牛强先生 职工代表董事：唐胜男女士 公司第七届董事会由上述9名董事组成，任期自公司2026年第二次临时股东会通过之日起三年。董事会中兼任公司高级管理人员职务的董事以及由职工代表担任的董事人数总计未超过公司董事总数的二分之一，独立董事人数不低于董事会成员总数的三分之一。董事人数符合《公司法》及《公司章程》的有关规定。公司董事会成员简历详见附件。 二、公司第七届董事会专门委员会组成情况 公司第七届董事会各专门委员会成员任期自第七届董事会第一次会议审议 通过之日起至第七届董事会任期届满之日止。其中，薪酬与考核委员会、审计委员会、提名委员会中独立董事均占半数以上，并由独立董事担任召集人，审计委员会召集人吴小丽女士为会计专业人士。具体如下： 董事会战略委员会：陈锋先生（召集人）、斯陈锋先生、闫建来先生 董事会审计委员会：吴小丽女士（召集人）、牛强先生、俞佳乐先生 董事会提名委员会：牛强先生（召集人）、闫建来先生、陈锋先生 董事会薪酬与考核委员会：闫建来先生（召集人）、吴小丽女士、陈锋先生 三、公司聘任高级管理人员及证券事务代表情况 总经理：陈锋先生 副总经理：俞迪辉先生、傅直全先生、斯陈锋先生、吴建松先生 财务负责人：江学芳女士 董事会秘书：江学芳女士 证券事务代表：何华燕女士 上述高级管理人员及证券事务代表（简历详见附件）具备与其行使职权相适应的任职条件，任职资格和聘任程序符合相关法律法规、规范性文件及《公司章程》的规定，任期与公司第七届董事会一致，即自本次董事会审议通过之日起至第七届董事会届满之日止，下届董事会可续聘连任。董事会秘书江学芳女士、证券事务代表何华燕女士均已取得董事会秘书资格证书，具备与岗位要求相应的专业胜任能力与从业经验，其任职资格符合相关法律法规的规定。公司将严格按照《上市公司董事会秘书监管规则》的要求，在过渡期内尽快解决董事会秘书兼职问题，调整至符合规则规定。 四、董事会秘书及证券事务代表联系方式 董事会秘书 证券事务代表 姓名 江学芳 何华燕 联系地址 浙江省诸暨市店口镇军联路 3 号 浙江省诸暨市店口镇军联路 3 号 电话 0575-89007602 0575-87605817 传真 0575-89007574 05

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）が新開発したブレーキパッドの「サステナ（新環境規制対応）パッド」が、2026年5月に国内発売されたMAZDA「CX-5」に採用されたことをお知らせします。

【開発背景】 欧州連合が定める自動車の新環境規制「Euro 7」（以下、Euro 7）では、ブレーキ粉塵も規制対象となります。当社が主力とするノンアスベスト（NAO）材は環境負荷が低い一方で、欧州で主流のロースチール材と比較し制動力の面で課題がありました。アドヴィックスは、規制値のクリアと高い制動力の両立を目指して進めてきました。

【製品概要】 本製品は、材料に石綿や銅を含まないNAO材をベースに耐熱性に優れた有機材や無機材、セラミックなどの配分を高め、環境規制値※1を満たしながら高い制動力を実現させた点が特長です。開発にはAI活用による配合パターンのシミュレーションなども活用し、多くの試験評価を経て本製品の優位性が認められ、製品化にいたりました。

アドヴィックスは今後も、電動化や環境規制などで発生する課題に対し、顧客視点で迅速なソリューションを提供し続けてまいります。

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）は、愛知県が推進する女性活躍促進施策において、2026年6月10日に「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」に認定されました。

「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」は、愛知県が、県全体の女性活躍を県と共に推進する企業に交付されます。「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」に認定されるには、「あいち女性輝きカンパニー」の認証を取得している必要があり、アドヴィックスは、2024年7月に認証を取得しています。

当社の女性活躍やダイバーシティ推進の最大の特徴は、女性従業員が主体となり、誰もが働きやすくなるための施策を考え、経営に提案し、実現していることにあります。例えば、女性同士がキャリア形成や育児との両立について気軽に相談・交流できる女性交流サロンや、先輩ママの声を盛り込んだ復職ガイドの作成、製造現場では女性ならではの視点を活かした高さや重さに関する作業環境の改善やマタニティウエアの導入など、当事者の声を大切にしながら働きやすい職場づくりを進めています。また、両立支援の取り組みなども評価され、2025年12月に「プラチナくるみん」認定を取得しています。

アドヴィックスは今後、「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」として、女性活躍に関する取り組みや知見の発信・共有を通じて、地域全体の取り組みに寄与していきます。

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）は、ドイツ自動車工業会（VDA）が設計した情報セキュリティの基準であるTISAX（Trusted Information Security Assessment Exchange）認証を取得しました。

近年、自動車業界においては重要な情報を他社と共有し製品を共同開発する動きが活発になっています。共有する情報の中には機密性の高い内容が含まれているため、サプライチェーン全体でセキュリティレベルの把握と高度な情報セキュリティ対策の強化が喫緊で求められています。

TISAXは、自動車業界のサプライチェーン全体で、情報セキュリティ水準を共通の基準で評価・共有するための業界標準の認証（評価）制度です。TISAX認証を取得することで、情報セキュリティレベルを客観的に証明できるため、顧客や取引先からの信頼性が向上します。また、共有プラットフォーム上で評価結果を確認することができるので、個社毎に審査や回答を行う必要がなくなり、取引開始までのプロセスを大幅に効率化できます。今回の本社拠点での認証取得を皮切りに、欧州をはじめとした各地域の開発拠点での取得を目指します。

アドヴィックスは、情報セキュリティ体制の継続的な強化に取り組み、お客様と社会から信頼される企業であり続けてまいります。

BETHESDA, Md . — January 14, 2026 — The Auto Care Association today thanked the United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce’s Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade (CMT) for holding a timely and important hearing to examine legislative options to strengthen motor vehicle safety, ensure consumer choice and affordability, and cement U.S. automotive leadership.

The association commended Chairman Bilirakis, R-Fla.-12, Ranking Member Schakowsky, D-Ill.-9, and members of the Subcommittee for their leadership and thoughtful consideration of bipartisan solutions that recognize the rapidly evolving nature of vehicle technology and its impact on safety, repair, and consumer costs.

In testimony provided to the subcommittee, Auto Care Association President and CEO Bill Hanvey emphasized that safe, affordable, and accessible vehicle repair is essential to highway safety and consumer protection, particularly as vehicles become increasingly software-driven and data-dependent.

“Today’s vehicles are computers on wheels,” Hanvey said, noting that manufacturers are increasingly restricting access to critical repair and maintenance data. “When vehicle owners and independent repairers are locked out of that data, repairs are delayed, costs increase, and safety can be compromised.”

Hanvey underscored the importance of including the Right to Equitable and Professional Auto Industry Repair (REPAIR) Act (H.R. 1566) in the safety title of the upcoming Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act. He highlighted that the bipartisan legislation, supported by 42 cosponsors and more than 83% of American voters, would immediately enhance safety by ensuring vehicle owners can choose where and how their vehicles are professionally repaired.

Key points from Hanvey’s testimony included:

Cost and safety impacts on consumers : Manufacturer-imposed data restrictions are forcing vehicle owners into franchised dealerships, where repair costs are, on average, 36% higher and wait times significantly longer.

Real-world safety consequences : Independent repair shops are routinely unable to complete even basic repairs—such as battery replacements or windshield wiper changes—without dealer-only codes, resulting in unnecessary delays and added risk for drivers.

Economic and workforce implications : Independent repair shops perform more than 70% of out-of-warranty repairs nationwide and are critical to local economies, workforce development, and vehicle uptime for working families and commercial fleets.

Cybersecurity and intellectual property protections: The REPAIR Act preserves existing intellectual property rights and cybersecurity standards  manufacturers use to deliver data to franchised dealers.

Commercial vehicle safety: With only about 5,600 medium- and heavy-duty truck dealerships nationwide, independent and mobile repair providers are essential to keeping commercial fleets operating safely, especially in rural and remote regions.

Hanvey warned that without federal action, the automotive aftermarket faces an existential threat that would lead to a vertically integrated industry, reduced competition, higher prices, diminished quality, and fewer choices for consumers.

“The REPAIR Act is pro-consumer, pro-safety, and pro-competition,” Hanvey said. “It simply ensures that vehicle owners can access the repair and maintenance data necessary to keep their vehicles safe and on the road—just as they always have.”

Learn more about the REPAIR Act and send a letter to Congress today at repairact.com.

BETHESDA, Md. – Sept. 10, 2025 – Great Place To Work® and Fortune magazine selected the Auto Care Association for the 2025 Fortune Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services™ List. Earning a spot at 35 on this list recognizes the Auto Care Association as one of the best companies to work for in the country. This is the fourth recognition the Auto Care Association has earned for great workplaces and comes in addition to earning the certification of “Great Place to Work” both in 2024 and again in 2025 as well as 2025 Best Small Workplace.

The Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services award is based on an analysis of survey responses from nearly 149,000 employees at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies in the consulting and professional services industry.

“This recognition is a direct reflection of our incredible team,” said Bill Hanvey, president and CEO, Auto Care Association. “Their passion and commitment make this such a special place to work. We’re proud to celebrate them and thankful for everything they do to make honors like this possible.”

The Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services list is highly competitive. Great Place To Work, the global authority on workplace culture, determines its lists using its proprietary Trust Index™ Survey to evaluate and certify thousands of organizations in America’s largest ongoing annual workforce study, based on more than 1.3 million survey responses and data from companies representing more than 8.4 million employees.

“We’re incredibly proud to once again be recognized as a Great Place to Work, now with the additional honor of being named among the best in consulting and professional services,” said Lea Diamond, senior vice president, people operations, Auto Care Association. “These achievements reflect the culture of trust, collaboration, respect—and most importantly, fun—that our employees build every day. Earning back-to-back certifications and this new recognition reinforces our commitment to creating an environment where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.”

Survey responses reflect a comprehensive picture of the workplace experience. Honorees were selected based on their ability to offer positive outcomes for employees regardless of job role, race, gender, sexual orientation, work status or other demographic identifier.

To learn more about working at Auto Care Association, view the association’s Great Place To Work profile or visit https://www.autocare.org/about-us/working-at-auto-care .

About Great Place To Work As the global authority on workplace culture, Great Place To Work brings 30 years of groundbreaking research and data to help every place become a great place to work for all. Its proprietary platform and Great Place To Work Model help companies evaluate the experience of every employee, with exemplary workplaces becoming Great Place To Work Certified and receiving recognition on a coveted Best Workplaces™ List.

About Fortune Fortune upholds a legacy of award-winning writing and trusted reporting for executives who want to make business better. Independently owned, with a global perspective and digital agility, Fortune tells the stories of a new generation of innovators, builders and risk takers. Online and in print, Fortune measures corporate performance through rigorous benchmarks and holds companies accountable. Fortune creates communities by convening true thought leaders and iconoclasts — those who shape industry, commerce, and society — through powerful and prestigious lists, events, and conferences, such as the iconic Fortune 500, the CEO Initiative and Most Powerful Women. For more information, visit fortune.com .

9月11日， 银企行合作赋能汽摩配企业抱团出海暨共建上海国际汽配永久展馆战略发展大会 在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店召开。本次大会是银、行、企三方协同的一次集中呈现—— 银行赋能给金融支持，行业商会做纽带，企业作为主体积极参与 。三方各尽其责、各展所长，上海国际汽配永久展馆的生态协同效应与平台优势进一步显现。展馆聚微成炬，让分散在产业基地乡镇里的中小汽摩配企业抱团出海，这束火炬，正成为指引中小企业走向全球市场的方向。

全国政协委员、全国工商联汽摩配商会常务会长杨英 在致辞中指出，当前中小企业单独出海成本高、渠道窄、风险大。永久展馆探索的 “基 地制造 、上海展贸、销往全球” 新模式，是商会服务全国会员企业的重要抓手。“永久展馆就是全国汽摩配行业抱团出海的事业起点。”她结合自身在印尼、越南建厂的经历坦言，单打独斗确实非常无奈，呼吁中小企业抱团出海。

上海市政协委员、上海新兴产业投资促进会执行会长、上海致盛实业集团董事长张润斌 表示，上海是我国对外开放的前沿窗口，嘉定更是中国汽车产业的高地。他坦言，中小制造业主体仍面临信息不对称、融资渠道窄、抗风险能力弱等难题，单靠企业单兵作战走不快、走不远。 上海新兴产业促进会将联动金融投资机构、产业园区和 各行业商 协会，主动参与永久展馆的资源对接与产业协同。

上海国际汽车城集团党委委员、副总经理陈杰 ，把汽 车城 25 年产业积 淀与永久展馆的落地逻辑讲得很透。 “无论是一个区域的发展，还是零部件企业发展，都离不开金融和资金的支持。 ” 如今汽车城已集聚上汽大众整车基地，以及理想、蔚来、舍弗勒等企业的研发中心。 他说， 永久展馆落在汽车城，看中的正是“客户就在身边”的产业生态——“好项目不缺空间，好项目不缺资源。 ”

全国工商联汽摩配商会会长、瑞立集团董事长张晓平 发表主旨演讲。 他给出硬核数据：据浙江省汽摩配行业商会统计，浙江全省中小汽摩配企业超过2.6万家，今年全省汽车及零部件产值有望突破1.4万亿元，大部分来自中小企业的配件出口和后市场。“浙江汽配产业的活力和潜力在哪里？在零部件，在中小企业，在出海。”

张晓平指出，中国整车出口今年有望突破 1000 万辆，未来中国汽配出口和海外配套市场将是超万亿级新蓝海。“ 不出海就出局。出海 是加法，不 是减法，企业的总部、税收、产能根基在国内。 ”他强调，中小汽摩配企业单打独斗的时代已经过去，“一个外商到温州、台州汽配制造基地，一天看 4 家企业，待十天也只能看 40 家。 在永久展馆，一天可以看一两千家企业。跑一家胜过跑百家千家。 ”

中国建设银行总行公司业务部资深副经理董宣忠 代表金融机构发声。他表示，建设银行推出“善建智造”“善建科技”两大专项方案，为汽摩配企业智能化改造、产能扩容、品牌出海提供全链条金融赋能。“ 金融正在加快转向服务实体经济。企业在抱团出海的同时，金融也在探讨如何走向全球，我们的目标是一致的。 ”

当天到场的银行阵容强大：建行总行及浙江、上海、广东、江苏、安徽、苏州等分行，农行温州分行、金华分行、丽水分行，民生银行温州分行，工行、邮储、浦发、温州银行瑞安支行等数十家金融机构负责人出席。一张覆盖跨境结算、贸易融资、风险规避的金融服务网络正在永久展馆周边织密。

银行给金融支持，商会做纽带、做服务，企业做主体、做产品——各出一块拼图，拼出的正是永久展馆这个“抱团出海”的产业生态。

永久展馆不仅是物理空间，更是链接全产业链的超级枢纽。当天，来自成都、青岛、山西、宿迁、廊坊、丽水、衢州、达州、南通、贵阳等全国各地的公交集团负责人近百人齐聚永久展馆，带着合作需求而来。通过“国企实力 + 民企活力，成就新质生产力”的协同发展模式， 新瑞立 已与全国 25 个省 110 家公交公司达成合作，公交系统的终端场景将与汽配供应链在永久展馆深度打通。

大会现场，永久展馆分别与河北再制造协会、 GL 出海联盟 达成战略合作，共同打造再制造汽车零部件展厅、GL出海联盟展厅。

从再制造零部件到出海联盟，从跨境电商到法律咨询、仲裁机构，永久展馆正在构建“保姆式”服务闭环，真正实现“进永久展馆，做全球生意”。

大会期间，滁州市委书记吴劲、副市长后其洁一行到访永久展馆参观交流，明确表示要加快推进滁州城市产业会客厅的打造，加快推进滁州公交公司与新瑞立的合作。这是永久展馆城市会客厅版图持续扩容的又一进展。

新瑞立 COO 徐本光发布年度发展报告：新瑞立在全国布局 265 家门店，拥有 30 多万个 SKU 和 1500 家战略供应商，合作客户超过 22 万，产品出口覆盖 100多 个国家和地区。

永久展馆组委会执行主任朱仲升介绍，展馆总建筑面积 5.3 万平方米，规划入驻 3000 家企业，目前入驻已超 2000 家，已建成 21 个城市会客厅。 12 月 1 日，永久展馆将正式全面开馆，届时全国汽摩配商会年会同期举行， 12 月 2 日 法兰克福展 在上海开幕，三大盛会能量叠加。 开馆前将冲刺 3000 家企业入驻，打造 100 个城市会客厅。

大会期间，巴西国际采购团一行 20 余人到访永久展馆，重点筛选中国质优价平的汽车零部件源头工厂，同时考察工程机械零部件供应链资源。 采购团对展馆“ 3000 余家源头制造企业、 365 天常态化运营”的模式高度认可。本次来访，搭建了中巴汽车后市场产业链合作桥梁，助力中国汽配企业开拓广阔的巴西市场。

组委会副主任、首席跨境电商专家李智荣拆解“一链一网一平台”数字化体系，为入驻企业实现全年 365 天、 24 小时不间断全球获客。新瑞立采购总监金丽敏发布国内国际双市场采购需求，将优先对接永久展馆已入驻企业。

答谢晚宴上，瑞安市惠华汽车机油泵有限公司董事长钱继续的一番话，道出了无数中小汽配企业主的心声。

“我们做机油泵的，产品藏在发动机最里面，车开了 20 万公里车主都看不到；我们的厂藏在小镇上，默默无闻。”钱继续动情地说，“我们这一行，一年要跑 50 多个展会，累得半死，但展会一结束，灯一关，人就散了。我们最缺的，不是手艺，是被看见。”

他把展馆广告贴在自己车上，跑遍杭州、宁波、广州。“ 以前是我去找客户，三天展会一散场，回去也没几个。现在是展馆让客户找得到我。 ”他说，一年 2 万元投入，换来的是 365 天的展示和全球流量对接，“这笔账，每一个务实的企业家都算得清楚。”

“相信才能看到，不是看到了才相信。”钱继续说，“我不是站在门口等客户，我是在屋里点一盏灯。今天这盏灯就是上海国际汽配永久展馆，灯已经点亮了， 365 天不灭。”

大会期间，钱继续又追加了一个展位。从“试试看”到“再加一个”，这位做机油泵的企业主，用最实在的方式投出了自己的信任票。

像钱继续这样的中小企业，正是中国汽配产业最真实的底色。浙江 2.6 万家中小汽摩配企业，九成藏在乡镇里，有手艺、有产品，却缺少被世界看见的窗口。让中小企业被看见——这是上海国际汽配永久展馆的初心。 当 2000 多家这样的企业聚在一起，微光便开始汇聚成星海。

但“被看见”只是第一步。 中国汽配品牌向上，正在经历从“被看见”到“被相信”的关键一跃。 永久展馆要做的，正是帮助中小企业在被看见的基础上，用 365 天不间断的展示、稳定的品质、银企护航的信用背书，一步步赢得全球采购商的信任。

截至本次大会，上海国际汽配永久展馆已吸引超过 2000 家企业入驻。 从 2000 家到 3000 家，从 21 个城市会客厅到 100 个，永久展馆的版图还在加速扩大。

银、行、企各尽其责，公交、保险、展会企业等生态伙伴协同共建，聚微成炬，众行致远。这束火炬，正照亮中国汽配产业从“单打独斗”走向“抱团共赢”、从“被看见”走向“被相信”的征途。

8月28日，政行企联动·走进上海永久展馆·赋能汽摩配企业内外贸一体化发展大会在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。本次大会由全国工商联汽摩配商会、上海国际汽车城集团、长三角汽车后市场产销合作产业链联盟联合主办，瑞立集团·新瑞立汽配连锁承办。

全国多地驻沪办、工信（经信）系统领导为主，工商联、商务、招商、开发区等政府有关单位负责人、各地商协会共同参会； 共商、共建上海国际汽配永久展馆100个城市会客厅。

从1月瑞安首站启航到8月入驻企业突破1700家，上海国际汽配永久展馆正加速成型。大会期间，永久展馆正式官宣： 银企战略合作千人大会定于9月11日在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。多位与会嘉宾表示，随着入驻企业持续增加，展馆核心铺位资源日趋紧张，9月11日千人大会后很可能出现一铺难求的局面。政行企三方正式从“走进”迈向“共建”。

上海市嘉定区人民政府副区长丁炯炯 在致辞中表示，上海国际汽配永久展馆作为赋能产业的重要载体， 已吸引1700家企业入驻。 展馆集常态展示、精准对接、专业招商、综合服务于一体，充分发挥嘉定汽车产业集聚和资源链接优势。 嘉定将持续优化营商环境，完善产业支持政策，为企业提供全周期、全方位的支持， 助力打通国内国际市场渠道，实现内外贸协同发展。

中国民营经济研究会常务理事、浙江省政府特约研究员、浙商研究中心副主任蔡晓春 在致辞中，一针见血地指出了大会主题的关键转变： “走进”是被动的参观、临时的使用；“共建”是主动的参与、长期的投入。

他指出，当前汽摩配产业面临整零协同不充分、出海体系化能力不足、跨界转型存在技术鸿沟三大痛点，解决这些问题需要“有为政府+有效市场+友好生态”三方协同。 共建永久展馆意味着三个转变：政府从管理者转变为赋能者，商协会从联谊会转变为资源整合平台，展馆从交易场转变为价值共创平台。新瑞立+永久展馆是双轮驱动，本质是产业互联网与实体展贸的深度融合。 只有三方联动，才能让中小企业“出海有保障、回来有港湾”。

湖北省人民政府驻上海办事处主任周彬 ，用湖北汽摩配企业抱团入驻永久展馆的实践，分享了驻沪办赋能地方产业内外贸一体化发展的经验。湖北正打造“ 武孝襄随十 ”万亿级汽车产业新格局， 依托永久展馆已落地十堰、襄阳两大会客厅，近百家鄂企入驻运营。 展馆对地方企业形成三重赋能：帮助立足上海、辐射全球，擦亮区域品牌；精准对接长三角主机厂与海内外贸易商；搭建商务洽谈平台助力内外贸融合发展。

全国工商联汽摩配商会会长、瑞立集团董事长张晓平 在主旨发言中指出，国内汽车市场已高度内卷，未来五到十年将迎来深度洗牌。而海外万亿级蓝海正加速打开，今年中国整车出口有望突破1000万台。 结论只有六个字：不出海，就出局。

针对部分地方政府担心企业“走出去”会导致产业空心化，张晓平算了一笔账： 出海不是减法而是加法，是“在国内做存量、在海外做增量”。 企业发展好了，总部、税收、产能的根还在当地。把企业搭载在永久展馆平 台上等于给企业 装上翅膀 ， 企业的市场越能海阔天空，企业的根就能扎得越稳，对当地“栽好梧桐树、养好金凤凰”就越有利。

上海国际汽车城集团党委委员、副总经理陈杰 介绍，作为全国汽车产业集聚度最高的区域之一，汽车城已汇聚上汽大众、蔚来、理想、博世等头部企业，每年举办200余场产业会议，持续凝聚行业核心力量。 依托高度集中的产业资源，永久展馆打造了一站式高效对接平台，外商单日即可触达上千家企业，效率远超传统考察模式。 放眼全球，汽车城正谋划公共出海平台，为企业拓展国际市场赋能，推动产业链抱团出海，形成全球化竞争合力。

上海国际汽配永久展馆组委会执行主任朱仲升 汇报最新数据： 展馆入驻企业已超1700家，11月底冲刺3000家。 总建筑面积 5.3万平 方米，已建成20个城市产业会客厅。传统展会三五天热闹，永久展馆365天细水长流， 200多批国内外商贸代表团，体现了蓬勃的产业能量。

上海国际汽配永久展馆组委会副主任、首席跨境电商专家李智荣 详解“一链一网一平台”线上线下闭环：3000家供应链为“一链”，全域流量网为“一网”，产业互联网平台为“一平台”， 七个维度流量来源实现全年不间断全球获客 。

新瑞立采购总监金丽敏 发布百亿采购计划： 去年采购超30亿元，未来5年将冲向每年百亿的采购额， 其 中出口50亿元，将优先对接入驻企业。 平台对外全面开放，入驻企业品牌将通过海外20多场专业展会持续曝光。

大会现场， 张晓平分别与国家外贸转型升级基地（上海嘉定·汽车及零部件）副总经理徐明、 星鼎荟中国汽车后市场企业家俱乐部 洪耿戈签署战略合作协 议。 这标志着永久展馆的“共建”朋友圈再扩容——嘉定基地带 来政策与口 岸资源，广东星鼎荟注入渠道与市场活力 ， 长三角和大湾区加强联动， 内外贸一体化发展再提速。

浙江省工商联原二级巡视员刘志义 用“五个五”为大会做总结： 五彩缤纷、五业并举、五富临门、五家兴旺、五站共进。

正如蔡晓春所说： “只要政府、行业、企业三方心往一处想，真正以共建者的姿态投身于永久展馆，就一定能在全球市场的星辰大海中开辟崭新未来。”

从“走进”到“共建”，这场政行企的双向奔赴正在改写 中国汽摩配 的出海叙事。大会现场同步官宣：银企战略合作千人大会定于9月11日在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。部分与会嘉宾表示，随着入驻企业持续增加，展馆核心铺位资源日趋紧张，9月11日千人大会后很可能出现一铺难求的局面。

浙江省工商联原副书记、副主席、一级巡视员，中国民营经济研究会常务理事、浙江省政府特约研究员、浙商研究中心副主任蔡晓春；

以及来自上海、天津、重庆、浙江、安徽、湖北、吉林、江西、河北、山西、四川等省级工信、驻沪办、贸促会部门有关单位领导，和广州、合肥、青岛、南京、长春、南昌、西安、太原、昆明、贵阳、包头、宁波、温州、湖州、绍兴、嘉兴、滁州、宣城、马鞍山、黄石、邯郸、开封、曲阜、綦江、永川、铜梁、扬州、宜春、九江、黄山、汉中、蚌埠、广元、淮北、济宁、南充、绵阳、丽水、烟台、伊犁州、枣庄、许昌、聊城、安庆、德阳、内江、宝鸡、盐城、诸暨、江都、乐清、瑞安、龙湾、瓯海、平阳、泗洪、桐城、余干、安吉、澄迈、大连金浦新区、清河、太仓、宁津、南浔、龙口等地方经信工信、驻沪办、工商联、商务、招商、开发区等省市县区相关单位领导。

8 月 24 日至 25 日， 2026 全球独角兽大会 在香港会议展览中心举行。这场以 “天生骐骥，创领未来” 为主题的顶级盛会， 汇聚 200 余家全球独角兽企业、 100 余家高成长科技企业、 100 余家投资机构及专业服务机构、 50 余家科研院校和政府部门，聚焦具身智能、人形机器人等前沿方向。 香港特区行政长官李家超出席致辞， 彰显对硬科技创新的高度重视。

瑞立集团旗下 广州瑞立科密汽车电子股份有限公司 （以下简称 “瑞立科密”，股票代码： 001285.SZ ） ，受邀出席本次大会。

8 月 25 日，机器人及具身智能独角兽论坛期间，瑞立科密迎来双重高光时刻：不仅获大会颁发 “ 2026 智能执行零部 件 领袖企业”大奖 ，更正式成为 中国机器人产业发展联盟首批成员单位 并参与授牌仪式。这一“奖牌 + 席位”的双重认可，是对公司从传统汽车供应链向机器人核心零部件领域跃迁能力的充分肯定。

奖项背后，是公司在高端制造领域近三十年的深厚积淀。瑞立科密已入选 国家级专精特新 “小巨人”企业、国家级制造业单项冠军 ，近七年 两次荣获国家科学技术进步二等奖 。

公司在摄像头、传感器、电机、轻量化压铸及精密机加工件等领域形成的硬件开发与软硬协同能力，与机器人对感知、驱动、结构等核心零部件的需求技术高度同源，为公司切入机器人赛道提供了坚实的现实基础。

这意味着，瑞立科密所擅长的，正是机器人从实验室走向量产所亟需的 “工业化能力”——这也是当前人形机器人产业最稀缺的环节之一。

在圆桌对话中，瑞立科密总经理 黄万义 指出： “人形机器人当前面临的最大挑战，并非技术原理的创新，而是 从样机到万台级量产过程中的成本控制、一致性与供应链韧性 。这正是瑞立科密在汽车工业中锤炼数十年的核心能力——我们有信心将这一 ' 基本功 ' 转化为机器人赛道的竞争优势。”

面对具身智能产业加速落地的窗口期，瑞立科密积极关注机器人赛道的投资布局，依托自身制造能力与技术积累，探索通过战略投资、产业合作等方式切入机器人核心零部件领域，稳步拓展第二增长曲线。

此次赴港参会，正是公司在全球化起航航线上迈出的关键一步 ——既是对硬科技实力的集中展示，更是深化产业链合作、对接前沿技术与资本资源的重要契机。

作为瑞立集团 的电子电控板块 ，瑞立科密将充分发挥瑞立集团在机电一体化、全球营销网络等方面的协同优势，以香港为 “超级联系人”和出海跳板，让中国智能执行零部件走向世界。

面向未来，瑞立科密将坚持技术创新，立足制造根基，以长期积累赋能机器人产业高质量发展，与全球伙伴共创具身智能新未来。

Ask most people how a damper is tuned and they will picture an engineer at a test track, adjusting something until the car feels right. That moment is real, and it is still where sign-off happens. But by the time the car turns a wheel, most of the decisions have already been made. Marcin Knapczyk, Chief Engineer at BWI Group, explains the process of damper tuning.

A long way from the car. It all starts with the customer and what they want to achieve. We normally work to a statement of requirements the size of a small book. It defines what the product needs to do and therefore what needs to be tested: durability requirements, hot and cold temperature ranges, all the different conditions the vehicle will meet in its life. Alongside that sits the performance target.

So the requirements are set. How does the system get into the vehicle?

Every project starts with integrating the system into the customer’s architecture. For semi-active system like MagneRide, that means aligning our software with their control environment and making sure everything communicates properly. Only once the system is operational do we begin calibration, adjusting control parameters to match the ride and handling characteristics the customer is after.

We have become more modular about how that works. We can supply a complete MagneRide system, including the dampers, sensors, ECUs and software, or just the individual components required. Some customers want full system delivery and tuning support. Others prefer to embed our control algorithms into their own ECUs.

Once you are up and running, what are you actually looking for?

We refine the system through real-world testing, evaluating ride comfort, body control, noise and vibration levels and overall vehicle dynamics, and we work towards whatever the customer wants the car to be, whether that is sharp handling for a performance model or a more composed ride in an electric SUV.

Underneath those targets are two things we have to control at once. Primary ride is body movement. Secondary ride is wheel control. MagneRide can respond in just a few milliseconds, which allows us to control both precisely. On a challenging surface such as an uneven country road, that responsiveness makes a real difference: we can maintain strong body control without introducing harshness from the wheels. Other systems often reach a point where they have to increase damping to control the body, and that leads to an overly stiff ride.

When the driver comes back with feedback, how quickly can you act on it?

That is what magnetorheological damping changed. Traditional passive systems use valves, which often require physical hardware changes during development. You are manufacturing and swapping out multiple sets of valves to refine the tuning, and that is time-consuming and resource-intensive. Ride Van, our mobile laboratory, travels and resides at a customer’s site (proving ground) where physical changes are made

With MagneRide we do not need to change any hardware during tuning. The damping force is controlled digitally through software, so our ride engineers can make changes directly from a laptop. That gives us much more agility in development, reduces cost and speeds up the entire calibration process.

How much of the final judgement is still subjective?

Subjective evaluation is a critical part of sign-off, and it is not going away. The complexity of modern vehicles, with all the subsystems in a modern chassis, makes it extremely difficult to do everything virtually, and an expert driver can evaluate the car across many conditions in a very short time. In subjective evaluation your body is the sensor, and you cannot simulate that. Even with all the AI we have now, it is difficult to describe what we are looking for.

How do you know when a tune is finished?

The bench test verifies durability and, in a more limited way, performance. The vehicle is where we verify that performance and define the nominal damper that is then reproduced in series production. After the ride session we have a master set, which is the evidence of what the customer tested.

How is simulation changing the shape of all this?

One of the biggest impacts is the reduction in the number of physical prototypes. One OEM told us they can now build ten times fewer test vehicles for a new vehicle generation than before, and a prototype car is extraordinarily expensive. The downside is that there is less access to prototype vehicles, which in turn encourages more virtual testing. It follows through to us as well: fewer prototype vehicles mean fewer prototype dampers to produce. Where simulation helps us most is FEA and CFD, predicting failures and avoiding them, which reduces the number of samples required.

So where does damper development go next?

It will continue to move towards bench testing. Using hardware in the loop to extend virtual testing and validate your models is much more cost effective and quicker than track testing, and you want the product to be as mature as possible before progressing to in-vehicle testing. But there will always be a need for physical vehicle dynamics testing.

The other direction is software. As EV adoption increases, expectations around noise and ride quality rise with it. Without engine noise to mask imperfections, every bump and vibration becomes more noticeable, and the added mass of an EV makes controlling body motion more challenging. At the same time the shift towards software-defined vehicles is accelerating the need for digitally controlled suspension that can be integrated and updated easily.

Battery electric vehicles accounted for 20% of new EU car registrations in the first five months of 2026, up from 15.3% a year earlier, according to ACEA . Add hybrids and plug-in hybrids and more than two thirds of new cars are electrified.

OEMs have a decision to make with electrified vehicles. Use regenerative braking; blending regen with the friction brakes as necessary. Or solely rely on lift-off regen, which is how one-pedal driving became a defining EV behaviour. The first maximises range but typically has poor brake pedal feel, the other has an unaffected brake pedal but is wasting energy.

The handover is where the driver feels the friction brakes take over from regen part-way through a stop. This is particularly noticeable in the last 10km/h of a stop because the electric motor needs to be rotating to generate torque. There are a multitude of variations that mean making brake pedal feel consistent is a real challenge. For example, when the battery is in a high state of charge full regen is unavailable, so the same pedal input produces a different response compared to when the battery is low. Battery temperature, brake temperatures, brake pedal force  – these all impact what blend of regen and friction brake is required.

An integrated electronic brake system, such as our iDBC 1-Box, decouples the brake pedal from the brakes themselves. A travel sensor and a pressure sensor read driver intention, an ECU decides how the demand is met, and a motor-driven pressure supply unit builds hydraulic pressure at the wheels. The pedal simply becomes an input signal where the force-travel characteristic/ resistance , or the feel, can be tuned through software.

Through this approach pedal feel can be calibrated to the character of the vehicle: firm and short for a performance derivative, progressive and light for a luxury saloon, and switchable between drive modes on the same car. Decoupling the brake provides better control of the deceleration whether the stop is served by regen, friction or a blend, and regardless of battery state of charge.

An added benefit of an integrated electronic system is that the motor builds pressure around three times faster than a vacuum booster. Reaching full pressure sooner in an autonomous emergency braking situation at highway speeds has a significant impact on stopping distances.

In urban conditions, the energy consumed during braking of pure electric vehicles generally accounts for about 30% of the total energy consumption of vehicle operatio n. So optimising regenerative braking can have a significant impact on a vehicle’s usable range. The limiting factor is often how confidently the braking system can hold friction out of the blend.

A coupled system has to bring friction brakes in early because the pedal is mechanically linked. A decoupled system can serve the majority of the stop through regen wherever grip, temperature and battery conditions allow, introducing friction only when demand exceeds what the electric machine can absorb. The driver feels one consistent pedal throughout.

What happens if the electronics fail on a decoupled brake pedal? Our iDBC was designed around fail-safe operation from the concept stage. The system is developed to ASIL-D and a direct hydraulic path from the pedal pushrod to the calipers remains as a mechanical backup. Even under a fault condition that disables every electronic system on the vehicle, the driver can still stop the car.

A brake system needs to be proven durable and safe across the full operating envelope, which is why the iDBC has been through high and low temperature programmes and a full winter test cycle on ice and snow at our low-adherence facility in Arjeplog, northern Sweden.

The nuances of subjective driving characteristics, such as pedal feel, steering weight and damper tuning, can be key brand differentiators, but noticed, in truth, mainly by enthusiasts and the engineers who created them.

Brake pedal feel in the EV era is different. Poor blending is not a nuance and it is immediately obvious to all drivers, whether they can name it or not. It erodes confidence in the car, and confidence is harder to rebuild than it is to lose.

The ambition, then, is not necessarily a pedal feel that impresses. It is a pedal the driver never thinks about. That is a higher bar than it sounds and it is easier to achieve when the pedal is decoupled and software controlled.

BWI Group’s Technical Centre Krakow has developed a bespoke artificial intelligence (AI) FEA tool. In a recent demonstration project it cut air spring development time from weeks to roughly one hour and uncovered a viable design that experienced engineers had already ruled out. We sat down with Miroslaw Siemieniuk, FEA Manager at BWI Group, to find out how it works, what it found, and why he believes the engineer’s role becomes more important, not less.

Q: Miroslaw, let’s start with the wider picture. Why have you and the team developed this AI-powered FEA tool?

A: That’s agood question. The automotive industry has changed rapidly over the last 10 years or so. Due to safety and electrification vehicles continue to increase in mass and at the same time development timescales are reducing. This is having a significant impact on chassis engineers, who are now being asked to land on tighter performance targets inside narrower programme windows.

Air suspension is a good example of where these pressures are being felt. Ride, handling, comfort and durability are governed by a large set of design variables that interact in tightly coupled, non-linear ways and resolving them is challenging. So there was a clear opportunity here to benefit from the potential AI has to offer.

Q: Walk us through how an air spring is typically developed today. Where does the bottleneck sit?

A: Typically, the starting point is a force-versus-displacement performance curve supplied by the OEM. This defines exactly what the air spring is required to deliver across its full stroke. Our aim is to try and develop a product that matches that curve as closely as possible.

However, due to the many linked interactions of the various components in an air suspension system, hitting that curve and satisfying a number of other conflicting requirements and constraints is rarely straightforward. Internal geometry, working pressure, sleeve material behaviour and reinforcement layout all influence the result. The current approach is iterative manual design, with each step supported by finite element analysis (FEA). For a capable team, converging on a workable design typically takes several weeks.

Q: How does the new AI-powered FEA tool change that?

A: In short,it replaces the repeated manual iteration with a deep-learning surrogate that evaluates design changes almost instantly. This is why Ai in engineering can excel. On the particular air spring used in this study, the full optimisation completed in approximately one hour. So, compared to a typical two-week baseline, that is a 98 percent reduction in process time.

Q: How is the deep-learning model built?

A: The surrogate is a five-layer deep neural network. Importantly, it has been trained on a set of 180 high-quality FEA datasets. Those datasets came from simulation models that had already been correlated against extensive laboratory testing. So we know the models have been physically verified and the network is learning from solid engineering data.

From that training set, the network learns the mapping between the air spring’s design parameters and its resulting force-displacement behaviour and is then used as a fast-evaluating surrogate for the underlying FEA. As with all simulation processes, accuracy and correlation are critical. Against the simulation reference, the model achieved an R-squared of 0.99. In other words, there is strong agreement between its predictions and full FEA outputs.

Q: What design parameters does the model currently optimise?

A: At present, the neural network is wrapped around five design parameters: piston radius, low support radius, sleeve thickness, design pressure and nylon fibre cord angles. A Newton-based optimisation algorithm drives the search, looking for the combination of those parameters that minimises the residual error between the surrogate’s predicted force-displacement curve and the OEM’s target. The resulting root mean square error came in at approximately two percent, which indicates that the expected system behaviour closely matches the target. Once an optimal configuration is identified, the candidate design is subjected to a final detailed FEA for validation.

Q: Did the model uncover anything that was unexpected?

A: It certainly did. During the manual phase of the project, the team had concluded that the target force-displacement curve could not be matched within the existing architecture without adding a specific structural constraint component.

However, the AI tool had a different answer. It identified a combination of parameters that met the target curve inside the defined parameter space without the additional component. Manual iteration had not highlighted it because the number of interacting variables put it outside what could realistically be searched by hand inside any reasonable programme timeline.

It is important to emphasise that this is a demonstration of feasibility. The project has not been signed off for production. Translating it into hardware would still require full testing and validation. But, I think it clearly demonstrates the value of AI in surfacing non-intuitive solutions.

Q: If this approach were ultimately validated for production, what would the implications be for OEMs?

A: The implications of developing a design that does not require this additional structural component are significant. Removing it would lower mass, reduce cost, simplify the assembly process and remove the tooling associated with that hardware. More generally, the workflow gives engineering teams a clearer view of where the limits of a given suspension architecture actually sit.

Automated roll control system can be connected and disconnected on demand while driving at speed

SARC removes the compromise between handling and comfort while also improving off-road capabilities

Its unique hydraulic architecture enables mode transitions at any suspension travel and even under load

BWI Group has developed an automated active roll control system. The latest update to the company’s SARC (Semi Active Roll Control) product features a new ‘automatic mode’ that enables a vehicle’s anti-roll bar to disconnect and reconnect seamlessly on demand while driving at speed.

The update addresses an increasing challenge in modern chassis engineering as vehicle mass continues to grow. With SUVs accounting for more than half of new car registrations in Europe in 2024, and BEVs typically around 30% heavier than equivalent ICE models, engineers are increasingly forced to compromise between roll stiffness for handling and compliance for comfort. Heavier vehicles necessitate stiffer stabiliser bars, which extenuates the issue.

SARC’s automatic mode aims to remove this compromise. By disconnecting the bar during normal driving, the system allows the vehicle to adopt a softer, more compliant baseline, only engaging the stabiliser bar when required. The control unit uses vehicle data, such as steering angle, speed, lateral acceleration and yaw rate, to determine when the bar needs to reconnect. During high-speed cornering, for example, it reconnects in less than 200 milliseconds and is imperceptible to the driver.

“Chassis engineers are continually trying to improve road handling and comfort, but the two goals are often incompatible,” said Bruno Perree, Engineering Manager at BWI Group. “The latest update to SARC removes that compromise, allowing engineers to optimise the roll bar purely for handling as it will be disconnected the majority of the time. This not only improves comfort but also adds significant off-road capability, which can be a key competitive differentiator in a crowded SUV market.”

At the core of the system is a compact rotary actuator paired with a fully self-contained hydraulic mechanism. The hydraulic architecture enables the bar to be connected or disconnected even when the wheels are unevenly articulated, which is something mechanical solutions typically cannot achieve. Automatic self-centring using the company’s EZ-Latch™ technology ensures consistent engagement throughout the suspension travel.

SARC is in production on several global platforms, most recently the GWM Tank series, where it is used to balance on-road composure with off-road traction. The addition of SARC’s automatic mode is expected to broaden its application to a wider range of SUVs and BEVs, where managing mass and maintaining ride quality have become central engineering priorities.
